p.src: Overview: A metric can always be made Euclidean through first order at one chosen point. Curvature begins where that coordinate freedom ends: in the second-order failure of neighboring local frames to fit together. We develop that statement in three stages. First come normal coordinates, then the covariant derivative and its connection, and finally the noncommutativity of two covariant derivatives, which defines the Riemann tensor and gives tidal gravity its invariant meaning.

ja: 概観: 計量は、一つの選ばれた点において一次の範囲で常にユークリッド計量にすることができる。曲率は、その座標の自由度が終わるところから始まる。すなわち、隣り合う局所系が互いに整合しなくなる二次の失敗においてである。この主張を三段階で展開する。まず正規座標、次に共変微分とその接続、最後に二つの共変微分の非可換性であり、これがリーマンテンソルを定義し、潮汐重力に不変な意味を与える。
zh: 概述: 度规总可以通过一阶近似在一个选定点处化为欧几里得形式。曲率始于这种坐标自由终结之处：即相邻局部标架无法彼此吻合的二阶失效。我们分三个阶段展开这一陈述。首先是法坐标，然后是协变导数及其联络，最后是两个协变导数的非对易性，它定义了黎曼张量，并赋予潮汐引力以不变量意义。

p.src: General relativity is difficult in a rather particular way. Its basic ideas are not impossibly obscure, but a calculation quickly becomes crowded with indices, derivatives, and symbols. More compressed languages exist: vielbeins, differential forms, spinors, twistors, and related devices can package long component equations into compact objects. Learning those languages, however, is itself a substantial task, and compact notation can conceal the machinery one most needs to understand on a first encounter.

ja: 一般相対性理論は、かなり独特な仕方で難しい。その基本的な考え方は手に負えないほど難解ではないが、計算はすぐに添字、微分、記号で混み合ってくる。もっと圧縮された言語も存在する。フィールバイン、微分形式、スピノル、ツイスター、および関連する道具立ては、長い成分方程式をコンパクトな対象にまとめることができる。しかし、それらの言語を学ぶこと自体が相当な課題であり、コンパクトな記法は、最初に出会うときに最も理解する必要のある仕組みを隠してしまうことがある。
zh: 广义相对论以一种相当特殊的方式显得困难。它的基本思想并非难以理解，但计算很快就会挤满指标、导数和符号。存在更紧凑的语言：vielbein、微分形式、旋量、twistor 以及相关工具，可以把冗长的分量方程打包成紧凑的对象。然而，学习这些语言本身就是一项繁重的任务，而且紧凑的记号可能掩盖初次接触时最需要理解的机制。

p.src: Maxwell’s equations offer the model. Written component by component, they amount to several separate equations. Vector notation collects them into divergence and curl equations, making the structure easier to see. General relativity admits analogous compressions, but the component method remains the dependable route when an explicit calculation must actually be done. We shall therefore keep the indices visible. Once their grammar becomes familiar, the conceptual path is much smoother, even though the arithmetic can still fill pages.

p.src: Symbolic computer packages can help with that arithmetic. Given a metric $g_{mn}(x)$, such a package can construct Christoffel symbols, Riemann tensors, Ricci tensors, and Einstein tensors. It can then substitute these expressions into field equations. This does not remove the need to understand what the objects mean. It merely separates the mechanical expansion from the geometry.

p.src: Response: The lecture singled out several fronts. Quantum gravity and the quantum physics of black holes were central problems in fundamental theory. Classical astrophysics and numerical relativity studied systems such as orbiting and merging black holes, where solving Einstein’s equations and predicting gravitational radiation require much more than blindly feeding equations to a computer. The same mathematical structures were also finding uses in condensed-matter physics and fluid dynamics. The historical point was equally striking: general relativity had moved from a comparatively small specialty in the 1960s to one of the central languages of theoretical physics, tightly connected with quantum field theory. p.src: A two-dimensional geometry is flat when Euclidean geometry works intrinsically: straight lines, parallel lines, triangle relations, and distance measurements all have their Euclidean form. It is tempting to say that flatness means $g_{mn}=\delta_{mn}$, but that statement is coordinate dependent. Even an ordinary plane has a position-dependent metric in polar coordinates. The correct statement is that a flat region admits coordinates in which the metric is constant and Euclidean throughout that region.

The right strategy is to construct a diagnostic from $g_{mn}$ and its derivatives. We want an object $R$ with two decisive properties: $\begin{aligned}
R=0
&\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{locally flat geometry},\\
R\neq 0 \text{ at } P
&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{curvature at } P.
\end{aligned}$ Most importantly, $R$ must be a tensor. A tensor that vanishes in one coordinate system vanishes in every coordinate system, so no coordinate search is needed.

p.src: Response: For field equations. Gravitational fields vary from point to point, so their equations must contain derivatives. At the same time, the equations should have the same content in every coordinate system. Covariant differentiation turns tensors into tensors and therefore permits differential equations whose truth does not depend on a peculiar reference frame.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:02:35)

en: This is the desired diagnostic. If every component of the Riemann tensor vanishes throughout a region, that region is locally flat. ja: これが求める診断法である。リーマンテンソルのすべての成分がある領域全体で消えるなら、その領域は局所的に平坦である。ある点でいずれかの成分が非零なら、座標のどのような変更によってもそこで曲率を除去することはできない。計算機代数システムは解析的な計量からこれらの成分を検査できるが、概念としては、平行移動が微小ループの周りで閉じないことにほかならない。
zh: 这就是所需的诊断方法。如果黎曼张量的每个分量在整个区域内都为零，那么该区域就是局部平坦的。如果任何分量在某一点不为零，那么任何坐标变换都无法消除该处的曲率。计算机代数系统可以从解析度规检验这些分量，但其概念无非是平行移动绕无穷小回路一周后无法闭合。

ja: 回答: 曲率は隣り合う位置を比較する。場が変化する長さスケールよりずっと小さい物体は、そのすべての部分でほとんど同じ加速度をサンプルし、ほとんど変形しない。拡がった物体はより大きな差をサンプルする。地球近傍で自由落下する細菌は無視できる潮汐応力を感じるだけであるが、講義の想像上の二千マイルの人ならひどく歪められるであろう。曲率は局所的な値をもつが、蓄積された変形は比較される分離に比例して大きくなる。  (講義時刻: 01:49:01)

One calculates them once as functions of position and can often see whether they vanish identically. Even then, this is far better defined than searching every possible coordinate system at every point.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:50:37)
